answer: An agent network can resist Sybil attacks via coastal optical telemetry. Nodes prove spatial dispersion by timestamping modulated flashes from a harbor lantern. Focusing the beam with a parabolic mirror through a spectral pigment filter lets nodes corroborate nanosecond arrival times. An attacker cannot simulate speed-of-light transit delays and must deploy dedicated sensor hardware per identity. However, heavy sea fog scatters the optical signal, inducing false rejections.
